title: World Models and the Law
abstract: arXiv:2611.29899v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Current AI may have a model of how we use human language, but this does not translate into a reliable representation of physical reality. World models promise to fill this gap by learning how an environment changes over time and predicting the consequences of an action, and they are already used to steer robots and generate explorable worlds. This article asks how AI regulation in three major legal contexts, the European Union, California, and China, copes with the distinctive challenges they raise. I propose a definition and a taxonomy of world models based on who or what acts on their predictions, and identify the risks of misplaced reliance on them. I argue that existing rules tend to cover world models but leave three questions open, i.e., action provenance, trajectory validity, and the weight of simulated evidence, and recommend ways to fill these gaps.

translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.29899v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：当前的人工智能可能拥有关于人类语言使用方式的模型，但这并不能转化为对物理现实的可靠表征。世界模型有望填补这一空白，它们通过学习环境如何随时间变化并预测行动的后果，现已被用于控制机器人和生成可探索的虚拟世界。本文探讨欧盟、加利福尼亚州和中国这三个主要法律体系的人工智能监管如何应对世界模型带来的独特挑战。我提出了一个基于“谁或什么对其预测采取行动”的世界模型定义和分类体系，并识别了对世界模型产生错误依赖的风险。我认为现有规则往往能够涵盖世界模型，但仍留下三个悬而未决的问题，即行动来源、轨迹有效性以及模拟证据的证明权重，并针对填补这些监管空白提出了相应建议。
tldr: 本文提出了基于预测行为主体划分的世界模型定义与分类体系，指出欧盟、加州和中国现有的AI监管规则虽能涵盖世界模型，但在行动来源、轨迹有效性和模拟证据权重三个方面存在监管空白，并提出了填补这些空白的建议。
en_tdlr: This article proposes a definition and taxonomy of world models based on who acts on their predictions, identifies three unresolved regulatory gaps—action provenance, trajectory validity, and the weight of simulated evidence—in existing AI law across the EU, California, and China, and recommends ways to address them.
